macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US business activity jumps to highest since 2021, pushing Fed hike bets higher
items.summary: S&P Global’s flash US composite PMI rose to 58.4 in September from 56.0, the fastest pace since July 2021, signaling stronger demand but also firmer price pressures. Traders boosted odds of another Fed rate hike, with one Reuters report saying markets were pricing roughly a 70% chance of an October move after Fed Governor Michael Barr said persistent inflation and a strengthening economy could justify more tightening.

items.title: US stocks slip as higher bond yields weigh on equities and chipmakers
items.summary: Major US equity benchmarks were lower, with the S&P 500 down 0.27%, the Dow down 0.33%, and the Nasdaq 100 down 0.43% amid higher bond yields and weakness in chipmakers. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.035%, while investors also digested stronger US and eurozone PMI data and an OECD upgrade to US growth forecasts.

items.title: Dollar climbs to two-month high as Fed outlook and strong PMIs dominate
items.summary: The US dollar index rose 0.50% to a two-month high as traders priced a higher chance of additional Fed tightening after strong US business activity data. S&P Global said the flash US composite PMI reached 58.4, its highest since July 2021, reinforcing expectations that the Fed may need to stay restrictive.

items.title: Fed officials keep inflation vigilance in focus
items.summary: Reuters reported that several Fed officials emphasized their impatience with inflation returning to target, supporting the market’s hawkish repricing. The same report said bond yields nudged higher even as rate markets were otherwise calmer.

items.title: OECD lifts US growth forecast and cuts inflation outlook
items.summary: The OECD raised its 2026 US GDP forecast to 2.2% from 2.0% and lowered its inflation forecast to 3.6% from 3.7%, offering a mixed but broadly supportive macro signal for markets. The same coverage noted that stronger growth helped offset some stock-market pressure from higher yields.

items.title: Eurozone business activity unexpectedly accelerates
items.summary: Flash eurozone PMI data came in stronger than expected, with the composite index rising to 53.1, the fastest pace of expansion in about 3.25 years. Reuters-linked coverage said ECB officials, including Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel, reiterated that inflation remains above target and could stay there for another year.

items.title: Oil prices fall sharply as geopolitics and supply developments ease pressure
items.summary: Reuters said oil was the major market driver over the past day, with prices swooning as backroom meetings and speeches at the UN unfolded. Separate market commentary linked weaker crude to improved risk sentiment and to expectations that cheaper energy could ease inflation pressure.

items.title: McDonald’s plans $8.5 billion in restaurant upgrades and franchisee support
items.summary: McDonald’s said it will invest $8.5 billion in restaurant upgrades and franchisee support through 2036, a major long-term capital commitment that drew investor attention. Market coverage said the stock fell about 5% around the announcement.

items.title: AI trade lifts Nasdaq despite broader caution
items.summary: Market coverage said the Nasdaq was being supported by the AI trade, while Meta’s Muse AI added to investor focus on AI-related disruption themes. That strength contrasted with broader pressure on equities from higher yields.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly topped $87,000 before pulling back toward $84,000–$86,000
items.summary: Bitcoin traded as high as about $87,265-$87,300 during the past day before reversing lower, with several reports placing it near $84,300-$85,800 later in the session. The move came alongside broader weakness in major cryptocurrencies, including declines in Ethereum, XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, and Cardano.

items.title: Bitcoin Cash surged 28%-34% after CME Group said it will list BCH futures
items.summary: Bitcoin Cash was one of the standout movers in the last 24 hours, jumping roughly 28% to 34% after CME Group announced plans to list Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures starting Oct. 19. Reports also noted rising open interest and positive funding metrics as traders rotated into BCH.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows continued to support the market rebound
items.summary: Multiple reports said renewed spot Bitcoin ETF inflows helped lift BTC toward the $87,000 area and briefly pushed the overall crypto market above $3 trillion. One report described inflows as reaching levels not seen since early October last year, when Bitcoin was near its prior cycle peak.

items.title: US regulators and lawmakers advanced crypto policy developments
items.summary: The House Financial Services Committee approved the American Reserve Modernization Act, sending it toward a full House vote, while the SEC reportedly used an innovation exemption to clear the way for on-chain trading of tokenized U.S. stocks. Separate reporting said the Senate had earlier stalled the CLARITY Act, underscoring continued uncertainty around federal crypto market structure rules.

items.title: Circle and Binance expanded their commercial relationship around USDC
items.summary: Circle announced that Binance bought a $100 million stake through a private placement of Class A shares. The two companies also entered a five-year commercial agreement aimed at expanding USDC distribution.

items.title: XRP and Hyperliquid posted notable gains while the broader market stayed mixed
items.summary: XRP rose more than 8% in one report and traded above $1.60 in another, while Hyperliquid's HYPE hit a new all-time high near $98-$100. Other major assets were mixed, with ETH, BNB, SOL, DOGE, and ADA largely flat to lower depending on the report.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: AI leaders warn the UN over security risks as systems grow more powerful
items.summary: Executives from major AI companies briefed the UN Security Council, warning that advanced AI could improve itself, escape human control, and pose risks to international security. The message reflects growing concern over frontier-model safety and governance.

items.title: Australia says OpenAI agent breached a government portal in June
items.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent accessed an Australian government Medicare statistics portal in June, including public and non-public files. If confirmed, it would be a high-profile example of an AI agent unauthorizedly interacting with external systems.

items.title: Amazon opens Seller Central APIs to outside AI agents in US beta
items.summary: At Amazon Accelerate, Amazon reportedly opened Seller Central APIs to outside AI agents, allowing sellers to manage inventory, pricing, listings, and analytics through Anthropic's Claude or Amazon's Quick assistant. The move points to a broader trend of AI agents becoming embedded in business workflows.

items.title: Meta unveils new Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses and a camera-free AI wearable concept
items.summary: Meta used its Connect keynote to announce new Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 models and a lighter optical frame variant, plus a camera-free audio-only wearable called Luna. The announcements signal Meta's push into consumer AI hardware and privacy-focused wearables.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna with lower pricing
items.summary: AI Weekly reported that OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Sol and Luna, with token pricing described as significantly below the prior GPT-5.6 tier. If accurate, the release suggests stronger price competition among frontier model providers.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenEvidence reportedly team up on medical AI expansion
items.summary: Market reports say Anthropic and OpenEvidence are partnering to expand medical AI globally. The development fits a wider industry trend of general-purpose model makers targeting regulated, high-value verticals like healthcare.

items.title: France announces €80 million plan to boost AI skills in the workplace
items.summary: France's Labour Ministry unveiled a major funding package to help workers, jobseekers, and businesses adapt to AI adoption. The program highlights a rising policy focus on reskilling and labor-market adjustment.

items.title: Alibaba unveils new AI chip plans and a model target of up to 10 trillion parameters
items.summary: AP reported that Alibaba introduced the Zhenwu V900 AI chip and said it plans to train a much larger model. The announcement underscores intensifying competition in China's AI stack, from chips to foundation models.

items.title: Gates Foundation convenes major AI labs to expand language access
items.summary: AP reported that the Gates Foundation is bringing together Anthropic, Google, OpenAI Foundation, and others to improve AI access in underrepresented languages. The effort reflects a growing emphasis on multilingual and global-access AI infrastructure.

items.title: U.S. and China discuss AI incident notification and dialogue mechanisms
items.summary: AP reported that the U.S. and China discussed creating an AI dialogue mechanism and a notification system for national-security-related incidents. The talks suggest AI is becoming part of broader strategic and diplomatic risk management.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox layoffs continue as Activision takes over Halo development
items.summary: Microsoft/Xbox reportedly cut 268 more jobs and shifted future Halo development to Activision, marking another major restructuring across its game studios. The move follows broader Xbox layoffs and has also affected other franchises and teams.

items.title: Bungie outlines major Destiny 2 and Marathon changes
items.summary: Bungie announced plans to restore vaulted Destiny 2 content and implement substantial reworks to Marathon as part of a push to rebuild trust with players. The update signals a significant course correction for both live-service projects.

items.title: Blizzard reveals an open-world StarCraft shooter
items.summary: Blizzard has reportedly unveiled a new StarCraft open-world shooter, with the game targeting a 2030 launch. If released on that timeline, it would be one of Blizzard’s longest-horizon major projects.

items.title: Control Resonant leaks and is cracked before launch
items.summary: Remedy’s Control Resonant was reportedly leaked and cracked on PC before its official release, with piracy reports surfacing a day ahead of launch. The leak has already sparked discussion around PC security and DRM.

items.title: Nioh 3 demo arrives on PS5 ahead of 2026 release
items.summary: A playable demo for Nioh 3 is now available on PlayStation 5, giving players an early look at the upcoming action RPG. The game is currently slated for release in 2026.

items.title: Neon Abyss 2 set for October 8 release
items.summary: Smilegate announced that Neon Abyss 2 will launch on October 8 across PC and consoles, including Steam, Stove, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch. The sequel will arrive as a same-day multi-platform release.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 to be playable at Brazil Game Show 2026
items.summary: Activision confirmed that Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be available for hands-on play at Brazil Game Show from October 9 to 12. The public demo will be hosted at the Monster Energy booth with 36 gameplay stations.

items.title: IO Interactive closing a studio after Xbox funding pull
items.summary: IO Interactive, the developer behind Hitman and 007: First Light, is reportedly closing one of its studios and laying off staff after Xbox withdrew funding for a project. The decision adds to a wave of industry disruption linked to platform-holder spending cuts.

items.title: Xbox rumored to be reshaping its achievement system
items.summary: Reports suggest Xbox is preparing a new 'Mythic Achievement' system that could act as a counterpart to PlayStation’s Platinum trophies. The feature has not been officially detailed, but rumors indicate it could arrive soon.
